notes:
CIRCUIT: a 48A current source driving a 53ohm shunt and a 59uF series capacitor, with a second loop made of a 44V source, a 56mH inductor and a 52ohm resistor. Top rail y~381 runs from the top-left corner (208,381) right through node A, on into V-DC 44V #0 (drawn + on the LEFT, - on the RIGHT), then L#1 56mH, then to the top-right corner (873,383). The right vertical drops from there to (873,507) where it meets the right lead of R#4 52ohm. R#4's left lead runs left to (575,498), where the wire turns down the vertical at x~572 to the bottom rail at y~613. The bottom rail runs left from there through C#5 59uF to node B and on to the bottom-left corner (218,604). The left vertical carries I-DC 48A #3 (arrow pointing up) between the top rail and the bottom rail. R#2 53ohm is a vertical shunt at x~408 between node A and node B. GND#6 hangs directly below the point where the bottom rail meets the x~572 vertical.

NET MAP (5 nets, 7 components):
  n1 = node A: the whole top rail from the top-left corner to the + terminal of V-DC #0, tapping the top of I-DC #3 and the top of R#2 53ohm. Terminals 0.0, 2.0, 3.0.
  n2 = short top-rail link between the - terminal of V-DC #0 and the left lead of L#1 56mH. Terminals 0.1, 1.0.
  n3 = right lead of L#1, through the top-right corner and down the right vertical to the right lead of R#4 52ohm. Terminals 1.1, 4.1.
  n4 = node B: bottom rail from the bottom of I-DC #3 rightwards, tapping the bottom of R#2 53ohm, to the LEFT plate of C#5 59uF. Terminals 2.1, 3.1, 5.0.
  0  = right plate of C#5, right along the bottom rail to x~572, up that vertical and right to the left lead of R#4 52ohm, plus GND#6 which hangs off the bottom rail at that same point. Terminals 4.0, 5.1, 6.0.

CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS:
  S1 (399,381) JUNCTION - the only CRITICAL site. Clean deg-3 T (kind=T, dot=1.8): the top rail runs straight through left-to-right and the R#2 53ohm column rises to meet it and stops. Nothing continues above the rail, so 'crossing' is not expressible; the only alternative, 'none', would strand R#2.t0 on a one-terminal net and leave the 53ohm shunt with no return path. Junction.
  S5 (409,610) JUNCTION - not flagged CRITICAL (flipping it does not change the terminal partition, because the third branch e17 is an 11 px stub of the same rail) but it is a genuine circuit node - node B, where the bottom of R#2 lands on the bottom rail beside the left plate of C#5. Recorded explicitly as a junction; the crop shows the column meeting a straight-through rail with no dot and no hop, and 'crossing' would orphan the 53ohm column.
  Non-critical sites S0 (591,329), S2 (162,495) and S6 (498,658) are the handwritten captions '44V', '48A' and '59uF' brushing a wire or symbol. Left at the default; verified that overriding them changes nothing.
  There is no ambiguous X, no solder dot and no hop anywhere on this sheet.

PORT / PIN FIXES: none of the six two-terminal parts needed one - the tracer picked the correct opposite leads for all of them (V-DC #0 p0 left / p2 right; L#1 p1 left / p0 right; R#2 p1 top / p0 bottom, its p2/p3/p4 being '53ohm' caption ink; I-DC #3 p0 top / p1 bottom, its p2/p3 being '48A' caption ink; R#4 p1 left / p0 right; C#5 p0 left / p1 right). No 3-terminal parts, so no pin-order risk.

GND WIRING - the one thing the tracer could not do (recorded via manual_nets):
  GND#6 came back with 'ports: NONE FOUND' and an unresolved terminal. Cause, confirmed with inkmap.py at (574,614) and edges.py: the bottom rail arrives from the left at y~613 and the x~572 vertical runs continuously from (572,498) down past that point to the top bar of the ground symbol at y~629. The tracer therefore traced the rail and the vertical as ONE bend (edge e12, (510,611)->(596,498), sites=[]) and pruned the 5 px of stub between the bend at y~613 and the GND bounding box top edge at y~618, so no edge tip ever landed on the GND box and no port candidate was created. The pixel dump is unambiguous: the vertical ink is continuous from y=592 through y=631 where it merges into the ground bar, and the rail ink joins it at y=612-614. The ground is physically wired to that node in the drawing.
  Because component #6 has zero port candidates, neither 'ports' nor 'merge' can reach its terminal (merge only unions terminals already present in the terminal map). I therefore pinned the three terminals of that node directly: manual_nets {'4.0':'0', '5.1':'0', '6.0':'0'}. Those three - the left lead of R#4 52ohm, the right plate of C#5 59uF, and GND#6 - are exactly the members of the tracer's net n5 plus the ground, so the grouping is unchanged apart from adding the ground, and the net is correctly named '0'. Nothing was invented: the connection is drawn on the page.
  The other reading (marking #6 'unconnected') was rejected: it would contradict the drawing and leave the whole circuit without a ground reference.

CLASSES: all 7 accepted. #0 V-DC (circle with + and - inside, '44V'); #1 Inductor ('56mH'); #2 and #4 Resistors ('53ohm', '52ohm'); #3 I-DC (circle with an up arrow, '48A'); #5 Capacitor ('59uF'); #6 GND (three stacked bars). The outer rectangle is the printed page border, not circuit ink, and carries no terminals.

UNRESOLVED: nothing.
